title: Jurisdiction under Brussels I bis
subject: Private International Law
note: Synthetic bilingual lecture transcript used to test the notes pipeline without recording. Written for tests; it is not a real class.

segments.text: Good morning everyone. Today we're going to study jurisdiction under the Brussels I bis Regulation, Regulation 1215 of 2012. This is the core instrument for deciding which court in the European Union can hear a civil or commercial dispute with a cross-border element.

Antes de empezar, una aclaración importante. Cuando hablamos de competencia judicial internacional no estamos hablando de la ley aplicable. Son dos preguntas distintas: primero, qué tribunal puede conocer del asunto; segundo, qué derecho aplicará ese tribunal. Hoy solo vemos la primera.

So keep that distinction in mind: jurisdiction is about the forum, applicable law is about the substantive rules. Students mix these up in the exam every single year, and it costs them a lot of points.

Let's start with the scope of application. Article 1 tells us the Regulation applies in civil and commercial matters, whatever the nature of the court or tribunal. It does not extend to revenue, customs or administrative matters, nor to the liability of the State for acts in the exercise of State authority, what we call acta iure imperii.

There are also express exclusions in Article 1(2): the status or legal capacity of natural persons, matrimonial property regimes, bankruptcy and insolvency proceedings, social security, arbitration, maintenance obligations, and wills and succession. Each of these has its own instrument or is left to national law.

Un ejemplo para que lo veáis claro. Si una empresa alemana demanda a una empresa española por el impago de una factura, estamos en materia civil y mercantil: se aplica Bruselas I bis. Pero si la Agencia Tributaria española reclama un impuesto a esa empresa alemana, eso es materia fiscal y queda fuera del Reglamento.

Now, the temporal and territorial scope. The Regulation applies to proceedings instituted on or after 10 January 2015. Territorially, it binds all Member States, including Ireland, and Denmark applies it through a parallel agreement. The United Kingdom, after Brexit, is no longer bound; for UK defendants we go back to national rules or the Hague Conventions where they apply.

The general rule is in Article 4: persons domiciled in a Member State shall, whatever their nationality, be sued in the courts of that Member State. Actor sequitur forum rei: the claimant follows the forum of the defendant. This is the default and it is based on the idea that the defendant should not be dragged to a distant court without a good reason.

Fijaos en que el criterio es el domicilio, no la nacionalidad. Un ciudadano estadounidense domiciliado en Madrid se demanda en España conforme al Reglamento. Y al revés: a un español domiciliado en Nueva York no se le aplica el artículo 4; ahí entran las normas nacionales por la remisión del artículo 6.

How do we determine domicile? For natural persons, Article 62 refers to the internal law of the court seised. For companies, Article 63 gives us an autonomous definition: a company is domiciled where it has its statutory seat, its central administration, or its principal place of business. Any of the three suffices, which means a company may have more than one domicile.

Esto genera una consecuencia práctica: el demandante puede elegir entre varios Estados miembros si la sociedad tiene la sede estatutaria en Luxemburgo y la administración central en París. Es una forma limitada de forum shopping admitida por el propio Reglamento.

Let's move to the special jurisdiction rules in Article 7. These are alternatives to the general rule: the claimant may choose between the defendant's domicile and the special forum. Article 7(1) deals with contracts. In matters relating to a contract, a person may be sued in the courts for the place of performance of the obligation in question.

Article 7(1)(b) then gives two autonomous definitions of the place of performance. For the sale of goods, it is the place where, under the contract, the goods were delivered or should have been delivered. For the provision of services, it is the place where the services were provided or should have been provided.

Esto significa que, en una compraventa de mercancías, el lugar de entrega atrae todas las demandas derivadas del contrato, también la reclamación del precio, aunque el precio se pagara en otro sitio. Esto lo dijo el Tribunal de Justicia en el asunto Color Drack, y es un punto que suele salir en los exámenes.

Article 7(2) is the tort forum: in matters relating to tort, delict or quasi-delict, the courts for the place where the harmful event occurred or may occur. Since the Mines de Potasse d'Alsace case, the place of the harmful event covers both the place of the event giving rise to the damage and the place where the damage occurred. The claimant chooses.

Ojo con una limitación: el lugar del daño es el del daño directo, no el del perjuicio financiero posterior. Si una empresa sufre el daño en Francia y luego su cuenta bancaria en España se ve afectada, el foro del daño es Francia, no España. El Tribunal de Justicia lo ha repetido en Marinari y en Kronhofer.

A question that comes up often: can Article 7(1) and 7(2) be used at the same time? No. The Court decided in Kalfelis that a court with jurisdiction over the tort claim under 7(2) does not thereby have jurisdiction over the contractual claim, unless another ground applies. Each head of jurisdiction is autonomous.

Vamos ahora a los foros de protección: las secciones 3, 4 y 5 del capítulo II. Protegen a la parte débil: asegurado, consumidor y trabajador. La idea es que estas personas puedan demandar en su propio domicilio y solo puedan ser demandadas allí.

Take consumers, Articles 17 to 19. The consumer must contract for a purpose outside their trade or profession, and the professional must either pursue activities in the consumer's Member State or direct activities to it. Directing activities is the key concept for online businesses; the Court developed indicators in Pammer and Alpenhof: international nature of the activity, use of a language or currency other than that of the trader's state, telephone numbers with international codes, and so on.

Si se cumplen los requisitos, el consumidor puede demandar en su domicilio o en el del profesional, y el profesional solo puede demandar al consumidor en el domicilio del consumidor. Además, los acuerdos de elección de foro previos al litigio solo valen si amplían las opciones del consumidor. Esto es examen seguro.

Now, the most important article for today: Article 24, exclusive jurisdiction. These rules apply regardless of the domicile of the parties, and they cannot be displaced by agreement or by submission. There are five heads.

First, rights in rem in immovable property and tenancies of immovable property: the courts of the Member State where the property is situated. There is an exception for short-term tenancies of up to six consecutive months for private use, where the courts of the defendant's domicile also have jurisdiction if tenant and landlord are natural persons domiciled in the same Member State.

Second, the validity of the constitution, the nullity or dissolution of companies, or the validity of decisions of their organs: the courts of the seat. Third, the validity of entries in public registers: the courts where the register is kept. Fourth, registration or validity of patents, trade marks and similar rights: the courts of the state of deposit or registration, and this applies even when the question is raised as a defence, since the GAT decision.

Y quinto, la ejecución de resoluciones: los tribunales del Estado miembro donde se ejecuta. Lo esencial que tenéis que recordar es que el artículo 24 se comprueba primero. Esto significa que, antes de mirar el domicilio del demandado o cualquier acuerdo de sumisión, debemos comprobar si estamos ante un foro exclusivo.

Article 27 reinforces this: where a court of a Member State is seised of a claim which is principally concerned with a matter over which the courts of another Member State have exclusive jurisdiction under Article 24, it shall declare of its own motion that it has no jurisdiction. Of its own motion, ex officio, even if the defendant appears and says nothing.

Un ejemplo. Un italiano domiciliado en Roma vende un piso en Barcelona a un francés. Surge un litigio sobre si el comprador adquirió la propiedad. Aunque el demandado está domiciliado en Italia, la acción es real inmobiliaria y el único tribunal competente es el español, porque el inmueble está en Barcelona. Si demandan en Roma, el juez italiano debe declararse incompetente de oficio.

Be careful with the scope of Article 24(1). It covers actions in rem, that is, actions that determine the extent, content, ownership or possession of immovable property. It does not cover actions in personam that merely relate to property, like a claim for damages for breach of a sale contract of a house. The Court said this in Webb and in Schmidt. This distinction is a classic exam question.

Let's talk about prorogation of jurisdiction, Article 25. Parties, regardless of their domicile, may agree that a court or the courts of a Member State are to have jurisdiction. The agreement must be in writing or evidenced in writing, in a form which accords with practices the parties have established between themselves, or, in international trade, in a form which accords with a usage widely known.

Two changes introduced by the recast in 2012. First, the material validity of the agreement is governed by the law of the Member State of the chosen court, including its conflict rules. Second, the agreement is treated as independent of the other terms of the contract, so the nullity of the contract does not automatically mean the nullity of the choice-of-court clause.

La sumisión es exclusiva salvo pacto en contrario. Es decir, si las partes eligen los tribunales de Madrid, solo Madrid es competente, aunque el demandado esté domiciliado en Lisboa. Pero recordad: la sumisión nunca puede desplazar un foro exclusivo del artículo 24 ni vulnerar las reglas de protección de consumidores, asegurados y trabajadores.

Article 26 is tacit prorogation: a court before which a defendant enters an appearance has jurisdiction, unless the appearance was entered to contest jurisdiction or another court has exclusive jurisdiction under Article 24. For weaker parties, the court must ensure the defendant is informed of the right to contest jurisdiction and of the consequences of appearing.

Vamos con la litispendencia, artículos 29 a 34. Si se presentan demandas con el mismo objeto y la misma causa entre las mismas partes ante tribunales de Estados miembros distintos, el tribunal ante el que se presentó la segunda demanda suspende de oficio el procedimiento hasta que el primero se declare competente. Es la regla de prioridad temporal, first in time.

The recast fixed the problem of the so-called Italian torpedo. Under Article 31(2), when a court designated by an exclusive choice-of-court agreement is seised, any other court shall stay its proceedings until the chosen court declares it has no jurisdiction. So the chosen court now has priority even if it was seised second. This reverses Gasser.

Una matización que el profesor quiere que recordéis: los artículos 33 y 34 permiten, con condiciones, suspender el procedimiento cuando el pleito paralelo está pendiente en un tercer Estado, por ejemplo en Estados Unidos. Es facultativo, no obligatorio, y exige que se espere una resolución reconocible en el Estado miembro.

Let me say a word about related actions, Article 30. Actions are related where they are so closely connected that it is expedient to hear them together to avoid irreconcilable judgments. Here the second court may stay, it is a discretion, not a duty, which is the key difference from lis pendens.

Para terminar, el método que debéis seguir en un caso práctico. Primero, ámbito de aplicación: materia civil y mercantil, fecha, y domicilio del demandado en un Estado miembro, salvo que se aplique un foro que opera con independencia del domicilio. Segundo, foros exclusivos del artículo 24. Tercero, sumisión expresa o tácita. Cuarto, foros de protección. Quinto, foro general del domicilio y foros especiales del artículo 7.

In the exam, if you jump straight to Article 7 without checking Article 24 and Article 25 first, you will lose most of the marks for that question even if the final answer happens to be right. The order of analysis is part of the answer.

Y una última cosa: en el caso práctico del examen del año pasado, muchos confundieron el lugar de entrega de las mercancías con el lugar de pago. Repasad Color Drack y el artículo 7.1.b. Nos vemos la semana que viene con la ley aplicable a las obligaciones contractuales, el Reglamento Roma I.
